FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.97
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` claims to sandbox-test proposed fixes, but the optional test command is executed unchanged inside the tempdir (`_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`) without rewriting any file arguments to the sandbox tree. In the actual caller shown in `immune_agents.py`, the command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. That path is relative to the real repo, not the sandbox copy. The sandbox only contains copied source files, not `bench/tests/`, and any absolute paths in test commands would still target the real workspace. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` creates a temp tree via `_create_sandbox(...)`, but never remaps `test_cmd` paths nor copies tests into the sandbox.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature does not actually validate the patched code under test. Best case, tests fail spuriously because the requested test path does not exist under `tmpdir`; worst case, if the command uses absolute paths or module discovery from the parent environment, tests execute against the unpatched real tree, producing false SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts. That directly undermines the fix-verification gate used by the immune pipeline to mark findings `verified=True`, so bugs can be marked closed based on tests that never exercised the patch.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when creating the sandbox, also copy the test targets needed by `test_cmd` and rewrite any source/test path arguments in `test_cmd` from real paths to their sandbox equivalents before invoking the subprocess. If path rewriting cannot be done reliably, skip tests and mark them not run rather than pretending they were sandboxed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: FIND — pre-fix and post-fix tool counts are measured on different analysis scopes. `evaluate_fix()` computes baselines with `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, target_path)` / `run_ruff(target_path)` / `run_bandit(target_path)` on the real single file, then computes post-fix counts on `patched_path` inside a sandbox that preserves the package structure and may change import resolution. The module comment explicitly says preserving structure matters because flat single-file analysis causes spurious import errors. Evidence: `_create_sandbox()` exists specifically to preserve package layout for post-fix runs, but no equivalent sandboxed baseline is used.
FOLLOW: Verdicts compare unlike quantities. A harmless fix can look HARMFUL because the post-fix run sees package-import context that the baseline did not, or a harmful fix can look SAFE because the single-file baseline already masked package-dependent diagnostics. This corrupts the key SAFE/HARMFUL decision used to close findings.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute pre-fix baselines in the same sandboxed project layout as post-fix, using an unmodified copy of the target and identical tool invocation scope.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_count_tool_issues()` collapses all tool failures to zero issues by `except Exception: return 0`. That includes missing binaries, timeouts, parse failures, invocation errors, and invalid output. `evaluate_fix()` then treats those zero counts as real measurements. Evidence: `_count_tool_issues()` catches all exceptions; `_run_tool()` encodes timeout/not-found as synthetic CompletedProcess values; tool parsers often return empty lists on parse failure instead of surfacing an error.
FOLLOW: The fix-evaluation feature silently fails open. If pyright/ruff/bandit are unavailable or erroring, both pre and post counts become zero and many patches get NEUTRAL or SAFE instead of UNEVALUABLE. The immune pipeline then may set `verified=True` on fixes that were never actually checked by tools.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — make `_count_tool_issues()` return an explicit failure state (e.g. `None`) on tool execution/parsing failure, and have `evaluate_fix()` mark the result `UNEVALUABLE` if any required tool could not be measured.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` only treats `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"` as fatal. Timeouts from `_run_tool()` are returned as `CompletedProcess(..., stderr="TIMEOUT")`, but `run_pyright()` then attempts to parse empty `stdout`, logs a warning, and returns `[]`. `run_ruff()` and `run_bandit()` have the same fail-open pattern for timeout/other malformed output. Evidence: `_run_tool()` returns sentinel stderr strings; the runners only special-case NOT_FOUND.
FOLLOW: Health scans and fix evaluations silently under-report diagnostics when tools hang or emit bad output. That can make health look clean and can mark fixes SAFE/NEUTRAL when the checker simply timed out. This is silently wrong output in one of the module’s core functions.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat `stderr == "TIMEOUT"` and non-parseable output from a tool invocation as tool failure, not as zero diagnostics; surface that in `tools_available`/evaluation state so the caller can mark the scan or fix evaluation incomplete.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the coordinator interface does not implement the documented “defect detect” capability as a callable feature. The file header lists four core functions including “Defect detect — classify findings by defect category”, but the public API only exposes `scan_health`, `evaluate_fix(es)`, `compute_pacing_signals`, and `EndocrineLayer.run()`. Category classification exists only as an internal side effect inside tool-specific runners; there is no standalone defect-detection function for arbitrary findings/diagnostics. Evidence: no public function or report field corresponding to function 2 beyond embedded `category` strings.
FOLLOW: One of the advertised endocrine features never fires independently. Any caller expecting a separate defect-detection stage cannot invoke it, and the brain receives only raw health-scan categories, not a dedicated defect-classification output. For a PoC that claims end-to-end feature coverage, this is dead/missing functionality.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add a simple public `detect_defects(diagnostics: List[ToolDiagnostic]) -> Dict[str, int] | List[ToolDiagnostic]` wrapper that exposes the already-derived categories, and include its result explicitly in the endocrine report if the brain depends on it.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: FIND — slow-model and large-response pacing thresholds use `sorted(values)[len(values) // 2]`, which is the upper middle element for even-sized sets rather than the statistical median. With 5 models this is usually fine, but the code accepts arbitrary lists and can mis-threshold when model count changes or failures reduce the list to an even cardinality. Evidence: `compute_pacing_signals()` uses this pattern for both durations and response chars.
FOLLOW: Pacing signals can trigger too aggressively or not at all around threshold boundaries, causing the insect brain to emit misleading `increase_timeout` / `degrade_relay` actions. This is quality degradation rather than total breakage, but it directly affects pacing decisions.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — use `statistics.median()` for duration and response-size baselines.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` reports empty `tools_available` when `source_paths` contains no existing files. It returns early with `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` before initializing tool availability for the known tool set. Evidence: early return occurs before the tool loop populates availability keys.
FOLLOW: The report cannot distinguish “no files to scan” from “tool availability unknown”, and downstream consumers expecting fixed keys for pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy get an incomplete interface. This weakens health telemetry and can break simple consumers that index those keys directly.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — on the no-files early return, populate `tools_available` with all known tools set to `False` or a consistent sentinel state.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` falls back to `source_paths[0]` whenever it cannot resolve a path from the finding description/fix. In a multi-file review batch, an unresolved finding is therefore evaluated against an arbitrary first file. Evidence: final line of `_find_target_file()` returns the first source path if any exist.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can patch and lint the wrong file while still returning a concrete verdict. That produces silently wrong SAFE/HARMFUL results and wrong `original_file` attribution for findings whose descriptions lack an exact path mention.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — if no target file can be resolved uniquely, return `None` and mark the evaluation `UNEVALUABLE` instead of defaulting to the first source file.
VERIFIED: TRUE
